newsitem.title: EASTERN EUROPE: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest - May13.
newsitem.headline: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest - May13.

text.p: REUTERS EMERGING EUROPE PRESS DIGEST FOR ADVERTISING & MEDIA
Weekly Press Digest from Central and Eastern Europe on Advertising, Marketing, the Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Markets
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

-- Saatchi & Saatchi Bulgaria, which posted a $2.6 million profit last year with a turnover of $21.8 million, has been named Bulgarias best advertising agency for 1996 by Advertising Age magazine in the U.S.. Adia, the local branch of Young & Rubicam, was rated second with $1.7 million profit for 1996 and a turnover of $7.7 million. (Kapital, May 5-11, 1997)

-- The Czech Association of Advertising Agencies and the Czech federation for brand-name products have criticised demands by Nova, the biggest commercial Czech TV station, to reduce the number of commercials on the public station Ceska Televize. They say such a move would restrict competition in television advertising and strengthen a near monopoly enjoyed by Nova. The Czech parliament is expected to make a decision this month.
(Hospodarske Noviny, May 6, 1997)

-- A Czech poster campaign for energy drink Erektus depicting the Pope covering his eyes from a giant pair of legs and a skirt caught in an updraft appeared on the streets of Prague this month. The billboard has the slogan "when you want more than you can get." The Czech Council for Advertising said it had received no complaints about the advertisement. (Pravo, May 7, 1997)

-- Rank Xerox CR is waging a battle against what it describes as incorrect use of the Xerox brand name in the Czech Republic. It's running ads that say Xerox is not a generic term and not all copiers are made by Xerox. (Strategie News, April 30 - May 7, 1997)

-- The winners of the best Czech ads have been announced by radio station Frekvence 1. The most engrossing radio spot was an ad for Harper's Bazaar from Stratosfera. The most effective ad was from HMS Carat for the drink Yo and the best billboard was for Marlboro from Leo Burnett Advertising and EQU Media.
(Strategie News, April 30 - May 7, 1997)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

-- ORTT, the Hungarian radio and television supervisory body, is due to announce the winner of the tender for the country's new "Two" commercial television channel. The channel will start broadcasting from 1 September, 1997. (NapiGazdasag, May 8, 1997)
-- Bulgarian National Television has taken two of its most popular economic programmes off air due to lack of funds.
(Kapital, May 5-11, 1997)

-- Publishing company Metro CR in the Czech Republic is launching a new daily paper which will be distributed free in Prague underground stations. The first issue will appear on July 7. (Lidove Noviny, May 9, 1997)

-- Czech television companies will soon sign agreements for next season's television rights to football matches. TV Nova is expected to hang on to the rights for Czech first division football, and Kabel Plus will make either direct broadcasts or air short clips from the three most interesting games of the weekend. (Lidove Noviny, May 7, 1997)

-- The Polish Prime Minister's Internet page has been broken into by hackers who changed its content. A government spokesman said the hackers had not infiltrated any other government computers. (Gazeta Wyborcza, May 7, 1997)
-- Polish printer Drukpress, controlled by Germany's Passauer Neue Presse, has taken over the Echo Krakowa daily. (Dziennik Prawa i Gospodarki, May 8, 1997)

-- Bulgarian National Television said it made a loss of some 100 million levs ($66,600) covering the April 19 general lection. The management is expected to decide on restructuring measures and staff cuts to stabilise the institution.
(Kontinent, May 8, 1997)

-- More than 75 percent of Czech citizens have heard of the Internet, 45 percent have heard of it but are not interested and 10 percent have used it, according to a survey by the agency Factum. Most Czech Internet users are under 30, at the top end of the income scale. (Pravo, May 5, 1997)

-- Publicitas Praha will run special sections on the Czech Republic in foreign newspapers in the next several months. They will run in the International Herald Tribune in May, the Financial Times in August, the Wall Street Journal, Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung and Svenska Dagbladet in October, Le Monde in November and the Wall Street Journal - eastern edition in December. (Strategie News, April 30 - May 7, 1997)

-- Euromedia CS, the publisher of Penthouse in the Czech Republic, introduced two new titles on the Czech market called Studio Eva and Kapital. Studio Eva is a monthly aimed at women between the ages of 25 and 50. Kapital is a monthly financial publication aimed at entrepreneurs and senior managers.
(Strategie News, April 30 - May 7, 1997)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

-- Johnson & Johnson is introducing the Roc cosmetic brand in the Czech market this month. The brand is expected to compete with Vichy and Phas from L'Oreal. An advertising campaign will begin in women's glossy magazines in the autumn. (Strategie News, April 30 - May 7, 1997)
-- Car maker Daihatsu has returned to the Hungarian market, which it left in 1994. The company is marketing two new models -- the "Move" and the "Gran Move". (Napi Gazdasag, May 5, 1997) *********
-- IBM Poland will start marketing computers equipped with Pentium-2 processors this week. The new hardware will be priced between 8,500 zlotys ($2,690) and 9,600 zlotys. (Zycie, May 7, 1997)

-- The number of new Peugeot cars sold in Hungary soared by 70 percent from 331 to 564 in the first three months of this year compared with the same period last year. The brands market share has increased from 3.0 to 3.3 percent. (Napi Gazdasag, May 5, 1997)
-- The Polish Kredytowy Bank, which is controlled by Allied Irish Bank, will launch a new VISA Electron credit card aimed at low income customers, a spokesman said. (Gazeta Wyborcza, May 7, 1997)
-- Polish digital mobile phone operator Plus GSM has signed a roaming agreement with Britain's DCS 1800 Orange system, Plus GSM said. (Rzeczpospolita, May 7, 1997)
-- The German-owned Billa supermarket chain has opened a superstore in Sopot, north Poland. (Dziennik Prawa i Gospodarki, May 8, 1997)

-- Tobacco company Rothmans has stopped production of Pall Mall cigarettes at its plant in Lublin, eastern Poland, and 300 workers are being laid off, the company said. (Dziennik Prawa i Gospodarki, May 8, 1997)

-- Dunlop has an 8.0 percent share of Poland's tyre market and plans to increase it by 2.0 percent by 2000, Dunlop's marketing agency SP Opony said. (Dziennik Prawa i Gospodarki, May 8, 1997) *********

-- Bulgaria's Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski opened the Plovdiv International Fair for consumer goods and machines and technology last week. Over 850 firms from some 40 countries took part. (24 Chasa, May 7, 1997)

-- This year's Czech international conference on database technology DB Forum 97 in Prague will run on May 22 and 23. Sponsors of the conference are Microsoft, SAS Institute, Oracle and Software AG. (Strategie News, April 30 - May 7, 1997)
